title: Graded failover deadband misalignment and priority resequencing — incident postmortem
creator: Aisha Khan
description: During a planned capacity migration we observed a cascade of graded failovers across regions that resulted in a sustained SLO miss for tail latency (~99th percentile) for 22 minutes. The root cause analysis shows a mismatch between our deadband thresholds for graded failover and the priority resequencing logic used by the inter-region router, which caused excessive fanout and inefficient shedding decisions under load.
detection: Alerting: multiple SLO-monitor alerts triggered at 2026-02-14T01:43:00Z (tail latency > 99ms threshold). Console dashboard showed increased cross-region fanout and a spike in 'fallback' routes. Pager duty escalated to on-call infra and routing-engineering teams.
timeline: 2026-02-14T01:38:00Z - Scheduled capacity migration started; 01:42:30Z - first latency spike observed in primary region; 01:43:00Z - SLO alerting fired; 01:44:00Z - automatic graded failover initiated from primary->secondary; 01:45:20Z - priority resequencing triggered, causing many requests to fanout to tertiary region; 01:46:10Z - secondary region experienced queue growth and began shedding; 01:50:30Z - on-call manually adjusted deadband thresholds to limit graded failover; 02:00:00Z - traffic affinity and priority resequencing reverted; 02:05:00Z - tail latency returned under SLO; 02:10:00Z - post-incident triage started.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations executed during the incident: 1) reduced graded-failover sensitivity by increasing deadband window from 10s to 30s to stop oscillation; 2) temporarily disabled cross-region priority resequencing so requests favored local region affinity; 3) enabled higher-priority static routes for critical low-latency customers to prevent shedding. These restored stability within ~22 minutes.
root_cause: A combination of configuration drift and insufficient coupling tests: (a) deadband thresholds for graded failover had been tightened in runtime-1.22 to reduce failover latency without updating the priority resequencer's hysteresis; (b) priority resequencing assumed the deadband would prevent rapid toggles and therefore rebalanced affinities aggressively when seeing small latency signals, which amplified fanout; (c) no integration test validated the joint behaviour of deadband + resequencer under a rolling migration scenario. The net effect: transient latency signals caused repeated graded failovers and multi-region fanout, overloading secondary/tertiary regions and triggering shedding.
impact_summary: Sustained SLO miss for tail latency (99th percentile) for 22 minutes affecting ~12% of production requests routed through the migrating shard. Several enterprise customers saw degraded UX for high-concurrency endpoints; internal dashboards recorded a 3.8x increase in cross-region egress and a 42% increase in per-token cost during the event window.
metrics: SLO: 99th latency breached for 22m (target 100ms, observed peak 320ms)
Affected traffic: ~12% of total requests for the shard
lessons_learned: 1) Component-level tuning must be validated end-to-end — deadband changes require resequencer hysteresis updates and correlated chaos tests. 2) Conservative defaults for graded failover are safer during migrations. 3) Observability must show combined signals (failover count + resequence events) in one dashboard to detect amplification early.
action_items: A-1: Add integration test in resilience-ci that simulates rolling capacity migrations with both deadband and priority resequencer active. Owner: Tom Nguyen. Due: 2026-03-05
A-2: Introduce a canary guard that prevents priority resequencing from reassigning >10% of active affinities within any 60s window; implement feature flag. Owner: Marcela Ortiz. Due: 2026-03-12
A-3: Revert runtime-1.22 deadband tightening and publish a compatibility note for runtime tunables. Owner: Runtime Team Lead (Priya Shah). Due: 2026-02-21
A-4: Create a combined failover-resonance dashboard (failover events, resequence count, cross-region fanout) and add an SLO composite alert. Owner: Observability (Luca Romano). Due: 2026-02-28

A-5: Run a targeted chaos experiment in staging that introduces transient latency while performing rolling migrations; include load patterns matching high-concurrency customers. Owner: SRE (Ethan Park). Due: 2026-03-08
A-6: Update runbook for on-call to include an explicit step to disable resequencer in case of rapid graded-failover oscillation. Owner: On-call Docs (Olivia Reed). Due: 2026-02-25
